    def validate_span(text: str, span: EntitySpan) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError when the span does not match the source text.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Source text the span was taken from.
    span : EntitySpan
        Span to check.

    """
    if span.label not in LABELS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown label: {span.label}")
    if span.start < 0 or span.end > len(text) or span.start >= span.end:
        raise ValueError(f"span offsets out of range: {span.start}:{span.end}")
    actual = text[span.start : span.end]
    if actual != span.text:
        raise ValueError(f"span text {span.text!r} does not match source slice {actual!r}")

    def normalize_span(text: str, start: int, end: int, label: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Snap AGE to its number and MONEY to the full amount.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Source text.
    start : int
        Inclusive character start.
    end : int
        Exclusive character end.
    label : str
        Canonical label. Other labels are returned unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, int]
        Normalized ``(start, end)``.

    """
    if label == "AGE":
        # Gold is "73", "73 years", or "73 years old". Keep the digits.
        while start < end and not text[start].isdigit():
            start += 1
        end = start
        while end < len(text) and text[end].isdigit():
            end += 1
        return start, end
    if label == "MONEY":
        # A span may start at "." or ",". Include the digits in front of it,
        # then the rest of the amount. Stop before currency words ("Rp", "kr").
        while start > 0 and text[start - 1].isdigit():
            start -= 1
        while end < len(text):
            if text[end].isdigit():
                end += 1
                continue
            # "." or "," only when a digit follows, so a sentence period stays out.
            if text[end] in ".," and end + 1 < len(text) and text[end + 1].isdigit():
                end += 1
                continue
            break
        if end < len(text) and text[end] in "kKmMbB":
            end += 1
    return start, end

    def covering_windows(
    pieces: list[tuple[int, int]],
    *,
    size: int,
    overlap: int,
    text_length: int,
) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Return character slices that cover every piece.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pieces : list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` offsets in order, one per token or word.
    size : int
        Maximum number of pieces in one slice.
    overlap : int
        Pieces repeated from the previous slice. Must be smaller than ``size``.
    text_length : int
        Length of the source text. The first slice starts at 0 and the last
        ends here, so a prefix or suffix with no piece is still included.

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` slices. A text that fits in one window is
        ``[(0, text_length)]``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        ``size`` is below 1, or ``overlap`` is negative or not smaller than
        ``size``.

    """
    if size < 1:
        raise ValueError("window size must be positive")
    if overlap < 0 or overlap >= size:
        raise ValueError("overlap must be >= 0 and smaller than the window size")
    if len(pieces) <= size:
        return [(0, text_length)]
    step = size - overlap
    windows: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    start = 0
    count = len(pieces)
    while start < count:
        end = min(start + size, count)
        char_start = 0 if start == 0 else pieces[start][0]
        char_end = text_length if end == count else pieces[end - 1][1]
        windows.append((char_start, max(char_end, char_start)))
        if end == count:
            break
        start += step
    return windows

    def merge_overlapping_spans(spans: list[EntitySpan]) -> list[EntitySpan]:
    """Keep the longer span when two of the same label overlap.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spans : list[EntitySpan]
        Spans from one or more windows of the same text.

    Returns
    -------
    list[EntitySpan]
        Spans in start order. A same-label overlap keeps the longer span, or
        the higher confidence when the lengths match. Different labels are
        both kept.

    """
    ordered = sorted(spans, key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
    kept: list[EntitySpan] = []
    for span in ordered:
        overlap_at = None
        for index, current in enumerate(kept):
            if span.label == current.label and span.start < current.end and current.start < span.end:
                overlap_at = index
                break
        if overlap_at is None:
            kept.append(span)
            continue
        current = kept[overlap_at]
        current_rank = (current.end - current.start, current.confidence)
        span_rank = (span.end - span.start, span.confidence)
        if span_rank > current_rank:
            kept[overlap_at] = span
    kept.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
    return kept

    def currency_spans(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Return character bounds of amounts written with a currency symbol.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Source text.

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` of the numeric amount, such as ``10,000`` in
        ``$10,000``. The symbol stays in the source text so encryption can
        leave it in front of the ciphertext.

    """
    spans: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    for match in _CURRENCY_AMOUNT.finditer(text):
        group = "before" if match.group("before") else "after"
        spans.append(match.span(group))
    return spans

    def join_name_spans(text: str, spans: list[EntitySpan]) -> list[str]:
    """Return one string per name, joining parts separated only by whitespace.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Source text the spans were taken from.
    spans : list[EntitySpan]
        Name spans in that text.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        Surface names. ``Ben`` and ``Parker`` with a space between them become
        ``Ben Parker``. A gap that contains other characters keeps them apart.

    """
    ordered = sorted(spans, key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end))
    names: list[str] = []
    block_start: int | None = None
    block_end = 0
    for span in ordered:
        if block_start is None:
            block_start = span.start
            block_end = span.end
            continue
        # Merge when the gap is only whitespace.
        if text[block_end : span.start].strip() == "":
            block_end = span.end
            continue
        names.append(text[block_start:block_end])
        block_start = span.start
        block_end = span.end
    if block_start is not None:
        names.append(text[block_start:block_end])
    return names

    def tags_from_spans(
    offset_mapping: list[tuple[int, int]],
    spans: list[tuple[int, int, str]],
) -> list[int]:
    """Return a BIO tag id for each token.

    Parameters
    ----------
    offset_mapping : list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` character offsets for each token.
    spans : list[tuple[int, int, str]]
        ``(start, end, label)`` character spans. Spans must not overlap.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        Tag id per token. Empty offsets are ``-100``.

    """
    tags: list[int] = []
    active: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
    for token_start, token_end in offset_mapping:
        if token_start == token_end:
            tags.append(IGNORE_TAG_ID)
            continue
        matches = [span for span in spans if span[0] <= token_start < span[1]]
        if len(matches) > 1:
            raise ValueError(f"overlapping spans at offset {token_start}")
        if not matches:
            tags.append(TAG_TO_ID["O"])
            active = None
            continue
        start, end, label = matches[0]
        tag_name = f"I-{label}" if active == (start, end, label) else f"B-{label}"
        if tag_name not in TAG_TO_ID:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown label: {label}")
        tags.append(TAG_TO_ID[tag_name])
        active = (start, end, label)
    return tags

    def spans_from_tags(
    text: str,
    offset_mapping: list[tuple[int, int]],
    tag_ids: list[int],
    confidences: list[float],
    source: str,
) -> tuple[list[EntitySpan], int]:
    """Decode BIO tags into character spans.

    An ``I-`` tag with no open span of the same label is counted and dropped.
    Spans whose slice does not match the source text are counted and dropped.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Original text.
    offset_mapping : list[tuple[int, int]]
        ``(start, end)`` character offsets for each token.
    tag_ids : list[int]
        BIO tag id per token.
    confidences : list[float]
        Score per token, parallel to ``tag_ids``.
    source : str
        Value stored on each emitted span.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[EntitySpan], int]
        Accepted spans, and how many tag pieces were dropped.

    """
    if not (len(offset_mapping) == len(tag_ids) == len(confidences)):
        raise ValueError("offsets, tags, and confidences differ in length")

    spans: list[EntitySpan] = []
    dropped = 0
    open_label: str | None = None
    open_start = 0
    open_end = 0
    open_scores: list[float] = []

    def close() -> None:
        nonlocal dropped, open_label
        if open_label is None:
            return
        label = open_label
        start = open_start
        end = open_end
        scores = list(open_scores)
        open_label = None
        open_scores.clear()
        if start >= end or not scores:
            dropped += 1
            return
        span = EntitySpan(
            start=start,
            end=end,
            text=text[start:end],
            label=label,
            confidence=min(scores),
            source=source,
        )
        try:
            validate_span(text, span)
        except ValueError:
            dropped += 1
        else:
            spans.append(span)

    for (token_start, token_end), tag_id, score in zip(
        offset_mapping,
        tag_ids,
        confidences,
        strict=True,
    ):
        if token_start == token_end or tag_id == IGNORE_TAG_ID:
            continue
        tag = ID_TO_TAG[tag_id]
        if tag == "O":
            close()
            continue
        prefix, label = tag.split("-", 1)
        if prefix == "I" and open_label == label:
            open_end = token_end
            open_scores.append(score)
            continue
        if prefix == "I":
            close()
            dropped += 1
            continue
        close()
        open_label = label
        open_start = token_start
        open_end = token_end
        open_scores = [score]

    close()
    return spans, dropped

    class LegacyNERShim:
    """Presents a Recognizer as ``NER.extract`` for Name, Money, and Age."""

    def __init__(self, recognizer: Recognizer) -> None:
        """Store the recognizer used for extract().

        Parameters
        ----------
        recognizer : Recognizer
            Span recognizer to adapt.

        """
        self.recognizer = recognizer

    def extract(
        self,
        prompts: list[str],
        entity_type: str,
        batch_size: int = 1,
        output_dict: dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, list[list[str]]]:
        """Return surface strings for one sanitizer entity type.

        Parameters
        ----------
        prompts : list[str]
            Input texts, one string per row.
        entity_type : str
            ``Name``, ``Money``, or ``Age``.
        batch_size : int
            Unused. Accepted so the call matches ``NER.extract``.
        output_dict : dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None
            Existing dictionary to update.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[list[str]]]
            ``{entity_type: [[span text, ...], ...]}``, one list per prompt.
            Adjacent ``Name`` spans separated only by whitespace are one string.

        """
        del batch_size
        try:
            label = SANITIZER_ENTITY[entity_type]
        except KeyError:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported entity type: {entity_type}") from None
        if output_dict is None:
            output_dict = {}
        result = []
        for prompt in prompts:
            spans = [span for span in self.recognizer.recognize(prompt) if span.label == label]
            extracted_texts = [span.text for span in spans]
            if entity_type == "Name":
                extracted_texts = join_name_spans(prompt, spans)
            result.append(extracted_texts)
        output_dict[entity_type] = result

        return output_dict

    def extract(
    self,
    prompts: list[str],
    entity_type: str,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    output_dict: dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list[list[str]]]:
    """Return surface strings for one sanitizer entity type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prompts : list[str]
        Input texts, one string per row.
    entity_type : str
        ``Name``, ``Money``, or ``Age``.
    batch_size : int
        Unused. Accepted so the call matches ``NER.extract``.
    output_dict : dict[str, list[list[str]]] | None
        Existing dictionary to update.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, list[list[str]]]
        ``{entity_type: [[span text, ...], ...]}``, one list per prompt.
        Adjacent ``Name`` spans separated only by whitespace are one string.

    """
    del batch_size
    try:
        label = SANITIZER_ENTITY[entity_type]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported entity type: {entity_type}") from None
    if output_dict is None:
        output_dict = {}
    result = []
    for prompt in prompts:
        spans = [span for span in self.recognizer.recognize(prompt) if span.label == label]
        extracted_texts = [span.text for span in spans]
        if entity_type == "Name":
            extracted_texts = join_name_spans(prompt, spans)
        result.append(extracted_texts)
    output_dict[entity_type] = result

    return output_dict

    def check(name_list: list[str], target: str) -> int | None:
    """For checking if a target name exists in a given list of names."""
    for i, n in enumerate(name_list):
        if finder(n, target):
            return i
    return None

    def finder(word1: str, word2: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether two names match after Unicode normalization."""
    encoded1 = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", word1)
    encoded2 = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", word2)
    return encoded1 == encoded2

    def make_names_dataset(save_path: str) -> None:
    """For making a new dataset of names for sanitizing names."""
    name_data = NameDataset()

    countries = ["US", "GB", "FR"]
    first_names = []
    last_names = []

    for country in countries:
        first_names = first_names + name_data.get_top_names(n=1000, gender="M", country_alpha2=country)[country]["M"]
    for country in countries:
        last_names = (
            last_names + name_data.get_top_names(n=1000, country_alpha2=country, use_first_names=False)[country]
        )

    # Get rid of duplicates
    remove_fns = ["Saba", "Lanka", "Deblog", "Donas", "Bk"]
    remove_lns = ["guez", "quez", "ecour", "Mai", "ü", "é", "Behal", "Bk"]
    first_names = list(set(first_names))
    last_names = list(set(last_names))

    temp = []
    for i in range(len(first_names)):
        flag = 0
        for rfn in remove_fns:
            if rfn in first_names[i]:
                flag = 1
                break
        if flag == 0:
            temp.append(first_names[i])

    first_names = temp[:]
    temp = []
    for i in range(len(last_names)):
        flag = 0
        for rfn in remove_lns:
            if rfn in last_names[i]:
                flag = 1
                break
        if flag == 0:
            temp.append(last_names[i])

    last_names = temp[:]
    save_fn({"first_names": first_names, "last_names": last_names}, save_path)

    def save_fn(dataset: dict[str, Any], fp: str) -> None:

    with open(fp, "w") as handle:
        json.dump(dataset, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
